A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LayerAnimate and contain readable main texts, figures, tables, equations, and supplementary material. Retained components and relocated material can be matched reliably despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original four-task benchmark results, component ablations, a 20-participant user study, and qualitative experiments, including appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 reports original six-task benchmark results, expanded ablations, a 20-participant user study, and appendix trajectory-error measurements and motion-score experiments.

M1.justification: v3 replaces first-frame-only segmentation propagation with iterative key-frame segmentation that incorporates newly appearing elements. It adds trajectory conditioning through a hybrid heatmap/offset representation and trains with different control modalities selected independently across layers. These substantially extend v1's motion-score and sketch controls. The motion-coherence filtering stage is also omitted from the specified pipeline; the underlying layer fusion and motion-based assignment mechanisms remain recognizable.

E1.justification: The four animation tasks in v1 expand to six through trajectory-conditioned I2V and trajectory-conditioned interpolation. v3 also demonstrates simultaneous heterogeneous controls across layers in Figure 6. The animation domain remains unchanged; the increased clip count is a setting change rather than additional domain coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds CogVideoX to I2V and interpolation, and AniDoc to sketch-conditioned I2V. New trajectory comparisons evaluate DragAnything, Tora, and Framer. SEINE, DynamiCrafter, LVCD, and ToonCrafter remain quantitative comparators, although SEINE disappears from the main qualitative comparison figure.

E3.justification: The reported corpus grows from 563K to 665K clips, training changes from 50,000 to 30,000 steps, and batch size increases from 32 to 96. The static threshold changes from 0.05 to 0.1 and the motion-score upper bound from 20 to 30. Sketch extraction changes from Anime2Sketch to Chan et al.'s extractor. v3 explicitly excludes motion scores from headline I2V/interpolation comparisons and specifies matched control inputs. Appendix B adds trajectory MSE evaluation. Both retain a 1K evaluation sample, without establishing identical membership.

E4.justification: v3 Table 2 adds layer-capacity tests and heatmap-versus-offset-versus-hybrid trajectory ablations. Motion assignment is examined through progressive motion-information conditions for both I2V and interpolation, replacing v1's simpler removal test. Appendix Figure 8 adds a motion-score sensitivity example. Conversely, v1's attention-fusion ablation, visual component-failure analysis, shot-filtering analysis, and sketch-style comparison are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Both provide point estimates and user-vote proportions; the changed values do not constitute a change in uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces LayerAnimate's reported results: I2V FVD changes from 98.86 to 87.96, interpolation from 55.69 to 59.64, and sketch-conditioned I2V from 40.64 to 26.64. Changed training and conditioning prevent interpreting these as same-setting gains or losses. v3 adds trajectory results, including appendix MSE values of 46.58 for I2V and 24.40 for interpolation. Ablation results, qualitative examples, and user-vote distributions also change.

T1.justification: v3 Section 3.1 introduces explicit mask-set subtraction and union-update definitions in Equations 1–2 for iterative segmentation. This is a limited addition of formal algorithmic definitions. The diffusion denoising objective is retained with revised conditioning notation, and neither version provides theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction and conclusion expand the central contribution from independent layer manipulation with motion scores or sketches to flexible composition of heterogeneous controls, including trajectories, across layers. The contribution statement and principal demonstrations now foreground simultaneous composite control, substantially broadening the claimed capability beyond the terminology change.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations of control informativeness, complementary heatmap/offset representations, and the benefits of increasing layer capacity and motion information. It removes v1's explanation of weaker sketch guidance and its explicit limitation concerning control of elements absent from the initial I2V frame. Resolution/duration constraints and possible real-world transfer remain in Appendix E. Improved training-data segmentation does not itself establish that the omitted inference limitation is resolved.

D1.justification: v3 documents four-frame key-frame spacing, CoTracker3 tracking on a 60-by-60 grid, an 80% masklet-consistency threshold, control encoders, and padded-layer masking. It specifies 10% mask dropout and 20/40/40 modality-selection probabilities, and changes reported hardware from 16 to 32 A100 GPUs. Conversely, v1's explicit first/last-half allocation recipe for interpolation is no longer described. Both retain the same project-code link.

R1.justification: The existing diffusion and controllable-generation survey remains largely intact. v3 adds CoTracker3, MIMO, DragAnything, and Tora citations, discussing trajectory control and contrasting animation decomposition with depth-based approaches. PySceneDetect and Anime2Sketch citations disappear. Framer's publication update is bibliographic; its new experimental participation is assessed under E2.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, curation motivation, and method exposition undergo substantial rewriting. Section 4 is reorganized around frame decomposition, layer controlling, and feature fusion; the application narrative becomes composite control. Terminology changes throughout from layer-specific to layer-level, and the surviving limitations move into a substantially reorganized supplement.

P2.justification: The teaser, curation pipeline, architecture schematic, and qualitative comparison are substantially redesigned. Table 1 gains a six-task structure, Table 2 is rebuilt, Table 3 is added, and the user-study display expands to six charts. The merging tree moves from v1 Figure 2 to v3 appendix Figure 7; a trimmed version of v1 Figure 7 becomes appendix Figure 9. Several earlier appendix displays are removed and a motion-score sensitivity display is added.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the evidence for controllability through layer-capacity and representation ablations, direct trajectory-error measurements, and broader comparisons with explicitly matched control inputs. These address weaknesses in v1's validation, while detailed control-generation and training procedures improve reproducibility. Removing the attention ablation and the initial-frame limitation reduces completeness, but the stronger experimental design and targeted validation provide a substantial net improvement. The judgment does not depend on treating changed-protocol scores as direct performance gains.
